subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a current-session-only model-callable self-compaction action, preferably through session_status, or keep compaction behind sender/control-plane boundaries until a different policy gate exists?
rationale: The missing implementation is source-proven, but allowing a model tool call to abort, compact, and resume active session state is a product and security boundary choice that automation should not decide.

options.title: Approve narrow self-compaction
options.body: Allow a current-session-only session_status compact action after the linked PR is rebased and refreshed security/runtime proof is available.

options.title: Require an explicit policy gate
options.body: Keep the implementation direction but require an operator or tool-policy gate before exposing model-originated compaction.

options.title: Defer to continuation design
options.body: Do not land the narrow PR and decide self-compaction only as part of a broader continuation API.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow self-compaction
recommendation.body: Allow a current-session-only session_status compact action after the linked PR is rebased and refreshed security/runtime proof is available.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history signal across session_status, gateway tool surfaces, and compaction-adjacent runtime work.
